entries.what: Layer streaming for LoRA fine-tuning: the frozen base lives in host RAM and streams into a small pool of pre-allocated VRAM buffers one decoder layer at a time, so peak memory is one layer rather than the whole model. Llama-3.1-8B + NF4 at 119.6 tok/s, 3.32 GB peak, on an RTX 3050 Laptop 4 GB. Published class limit for that hardware was 1.3B.
why_it_matters_here: SAME VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE, arrived at independently. Their words: 'Streaming fails silently: sever the gradient path and the loss still goes down, because the upper layers keep learning. So the bar was never close enough.' They verified bit-exact against ordinary training - max difference 0.0 across nine architectures - rather than trusting a metric that moves in the right direction. That is our oracle argument applied to training.

The protocol caught a real defect: 0.94 divergence with byte-identical weights AND byte-identical adapters, no crash, no warning, a healthy-looking loss curve. A green signal that had established nothing - the exact failure class this session kept hitting.
They discarded a flattering benchmark that 'turned out to be measuring the driver, not the model'. We threw away three p=0.000 rows for the same reason: they measured the harness.

Technically composable: layer streaming raises the ceiling on WHICH model fits, verified search raises the floor on what comes back. On a 48 GB W7900 it would put 70B-class models inside the breadth table without changing anything in the loop, since nothing there knows what produced a candidate.
